findings.issue: Nothing ever maintains the SyncedEntity audit columns. WakeelDb does not override SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync, so CreatedAt/UpdatedAt default to default(DateTime) and OriginDevice to "" / RowVersion to 0 unless every future caller remembers to set them by hand. Core's own FinancialCycleService.EnsureCurrentCycleAsync is already an example. Verified empirically on a fresh migrated database: the financial_cycles row it inserts is `created_at=0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z updated_at=0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z origin_device='' row_version=0`, and because the change_log trigger writes `at = NEW.created_at` / `NEW.updated_at` and `device = NEW.origin_device`, the resulting change_log row is `financial_cycles I at=0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z device=''`. ARCHITECTURE.md §6 builds the whole "من تاريخ إلى تاريخ" export on change_log.at and the per-row device, so every row written this way is invisible to a date-range sync export and unattributable; DATA-MODEL.md §0 also requires row_version to increment on every local edit, which never happens. The existing test MultipleUpdates_EachWriteASeparateChangeLogRow only counts rows, so it passes with 0001-01-01 timestamps.
findings.fix: Override SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync in WakeelDb: iterate ChangeTracker.Entries<SyncedEntity>(); for EntityState.Added set CreatedAt = UpdatedAt = clock.UtcNow, RowVersion = 1 and OriginDevice = the local device id when it is empty; for EntityState.Modified set UpdatedAt = clock.UtcNow and RowVersion++. Inject IClock and the local device id (installation.device_id, read once per session) into WakeelDb via DbContextOptions or a small WakeelDbContextState service constructed in DbSession.OpenCore. Then add a test asserting that a row inserted and then updated through a service has created_at != updated_at, row_version == 2, a non-empty origin_device, and a change_log row whose `at` equals the row's updated_at.

findings.issue: The "no number with a date earlier than the last issued number" rule (AGREEMENT item 5, ARCHITECTURE.md §5) is only enforced within the same year, because the official_numbers row is looked up with `n.Kind == kind && n.Year == year`. If no row exists for the earlier year, the check is skipped entirely and a backdated official number is issued into the official register. Verified: issuing for 2027-03-05 produces `20270305/12001`, and a subsequent call for 2026-11-20 succeeds and produces `20261120/12001` with ClockVerdict.Ok. The clock check is only defence in depth (it is a separate, caller-supplied value — see the related finding), so this rule is currently unenforced across a year boundary.
findings.fix: Before the per-year row lookup, read the global watermark for the kind: `var lastDate = await db.OfficialNumbers.Where(n => n.Kind == kind).MaxAsync(n => (DateTime?)n.LastDate, ct);` and throw when `lastDate is not null && today < lastDate.Value.Date`. Keep the existing per-(kind, year) row for the sequence itself. Add a test: issue for 2027-03-05, then assert IssueAsync for 2026-11-20 throws.

findings.issue: The SqliteException arm almost never fires in practice. EF Core wraps every SaveChanges provider failure in DbUpdateException with the SqliteException as InnerException, so real database failures fall through to the "unknown" bucket. Verified: a UNIQUE-constraint violation on SaveChanges produces `DbUpdateException / inner=SqliteException` and ErrorMapper returns "حدث خطأ غير متوقع" instead of the data-specific message and action. Spec item 4 explicitly names SqliteException as one of the mapped cases.
findings.fix: Unwrap before matching: at the top of Map, walk the exception chain (`for (var e = exception; e is not null; e = e.InnerException)`) and match on the first type the switch recognises, or add an explicit `DbUpdateException due when due.InnerException is not null => Map(due.InnerException)` arm (plus AggregateException/TargetInvocationException). Add a test that maps a DbUpdateException wrapping a SqliteException and asserts it gets the same TitleAr as a bare SqliteException.

findings.issue: Parse is brittle against any value it did not itself write. It blindly slices the last character (`v.AsSpan(0, v.Length - 1)`) and then requires exactly `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffffff`. An empty string throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException; any value written by raw SQL (`datetime('now')` → "2026-09-15 12:00:00", `strftime('...%fZ')` → 3 fractional digits), by a restore from a backup produced by a different build, or by the sync-import layer (B6) applying rows with raw SQL, throws FormatException on every subsequent read of that table. Neither exception is mapped by ErrorMapper, so it surfaces as "حدث خطأ غير متوقع". This also blocks the natural fix for the change_log trigger timestamps (using strftime in the trigger), because ChangeLogEntry.At would then fail to materialise.
findings.fix: Make Parse tolerant: guard `string.IsNullOrEmpty(v)`, then `DateTime.TryParseExact(v, new[]{"yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffffffZ","yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ","yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ","yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"}, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.AdjustToUniversal | DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal, out var parsed)` and fall back to `DateTime.Parse(v, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.AdjustToUniversal | DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal)`, always finishing with SpecifyKind(Utc). Add tests for the 3-digit, no-fraction and space-separated forms.

findings.issue: All 44 change_log AFTER UPDATE triggers write `device = NEW.origin_device`, i.e. the device that ORIGINALLY CREATED the row, not the device that made the change being logged. When device B edits a row created by device A, the change log claims A made the change. change_log.device is the attribution the B6 sync engine and the conflict view (ARCHITECTURE.md §6) will build on, and origin_device is already available on the row itself, so the column carries no information as written. The same triggers also take `at` from the application-supplied created_at/updated_at rather than the actual time of the change (see the SaveChanges finding).
findings.fix: Change the trigger body to record the local device, e.g. `VALUES ('parties', NEW.id, 'U', NEW.updated_at, COALESCE((SELECT device_id FROM installation LIMIT 1), NEW.origin_device))` for all 44 update triggers (and keep NEW.origin_device only for the insert triggers, where the two coincide). Confirm the intended semantics with the supervisor first, since DATA-MODEL.md §11 does not spell the column out; then add a test that updates a row whose origin_device differs from installation.device_id and asserts change_log.device is the local device.

findings.issue: Unique indexes on soft-deleted tables are not filtered on `deleted_at IS NULL`, while the EF global query filter hides soft-deleted rows — so an existence check in C# can return "not found" for a row the index still enforces. Verified: soft-delete the current financial cycle, then call FinancialCycleService.EnsureCurrentCycleAsync again for a date in the same cycle; the filtered lookup `FirstOrDefaultAsync(c => c.StartDate == bounds.StartDate)` misses the hidden row and the insert fails with `DbUpdateException / SQLite Error 19: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: financial_cycles.start_date'`, which ErrorMapper renders as "حدث خطأ غير متوقع". ux_assets_inventory_number has the same shape (an asset's inventory number can never be reused after a mistaken soft delete, with no explanatory message).
findings.fix: Add `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` to ux_financial_cycles_start_date and ux_assets_inventory_number (SQLite supports partial indexes), and independently make EnsureCurrentCycleAsync's lookup `db.FinancialCycles.IgnoreDeleted().FirstOrDefaultAsync(c => c.StartDate == bounds.StartDate ...)` so it cannot try to insert over a hidden row. Leave ux_correspondence_official_number unfiltered (official numbers must stay unique forever) but document that choice in the SQL. Add a test covering the soft-delete-then-re-ensure path.

findings.issue: Seventeen column names deviate from the binding DATA-MODEL.md by gaining a `_json` suffix: agenda_json, asset_ids_json, cc_json, changes_json, counted_json, counts_json, details_json, fields_json, filters_json, items_json, ours_json, overrides_json, readiness_json, sections_json, theirs_json, totals_json, words_json (DATA-MODEL names them agenda, asset_ids, cc, changes, counted, counts, details, fields, filters, items, ours, overrides, readiness, sections, theirs, totals, words). The deviation is not even internally consistent: restore_log keeps `details` while audit_log becomes `details_json`. DATA-MODEL.md is declared "مرجع ملزم لكل حزم العمل", and ARCHITECTURE.md §3 requires the admin tool to be able to open any installation's database for maintenance, so it will read these names from the document.
findings.fix: Either rename the 17 columns in 0001_initial.sql to the DATA-MODEL spellings and add `.HasColumnName("cc")`-style overrides in WakeelDb.ConfigureTablesAndKeys for the C# properties that keep the Json suffix, or get the supervisor to amend DATA-MODEL.md to the _json spelling. Do not leave the two out of sync. Whichever way it goes, make restore_log.details consistent with audit_log.

findings.issue: IssueAsync takes ClockVerdict as a required caller-supplied parameter, so nothing in Core guarantees the ARCHITECTURE.md §9 clock check actually ran at issuance — a caller can pass ClockVerdict.Ok unconditionally and the §9 guarantee ("عند كل تشغيل وإصدار رقم") silently disappears. The spec also gives the signature as Issue(kind, now). Combined with the cross-year backdating gap above, backdated official numbers currently have no enforced barrier inside Core.
findings.fix: Keep the explicit-verdict overload for testability but make the primary entry point `IssueAsync(InOutDirection kind, DateTime now, CancellationToken)` that calls IClockCheckService.CheckAsync(now) itself and refuses on anything but Ok — inject IClockCheckService into OfficialNumberService. Update the existing NumberingTests to use the two-argument overload with a seeded clock_checks history, keeping one test for the explicit-verdict path.

findings.issue: audit_log has no change_log trigger and no sync columns, but DATA-MODEL.md §1 annotates it "يُزامَن كقراءة فقط" (synced, read-only). As built, the audit trail never reaches the other office PC. Similarly document_pages and document_links carry no id/sync columns and no triggers, so a synced `documents` row arrives on the second PC without its OCR page text or its entity links, breaking search and document navigation there (ARCHITECTURE.md §8).
findings.fix: Raise both with the supervisor as DATA-MODEL clarifications. The cheapest resolution consistent with the document: export audit_log by its own `at` range in B6 rather than via change_log (document that decision in the SQL header comment), and give document_pages/document_links either sync columns + triggers or an explicit line in DATA-MODEL saying they are re-derived locally after import.

findings.issue: No guard against opening a database created by a newer build: Migrate applies only scripts not yet recorded and never checks whether schema_versions already holds a version higher than the highest embedded script. An older الوكيل run against a newer wakeel.db would proceed with a mismatched EF model against official records. Separately, GetCurrentVersion calls EnsureVersionsTable, so a read-only inspection has a table-creating side effect.
findings.fix: In Migrate, after GetAppliedVersions, compute max(applied) and max(embedded) and throw a clear InvalidOperationException when applied > embedded (ErrorMapper will render it, and the UI can show a "هذه البيانات أنشأها إصدار أحدث" card). Split GetCurrentVersion into a pure read that returns 0 when schema_versions does not exist.

findings.issue: IssueAsync calls db.SaveChangesAsync() itself, which flushes every other pending tracked change in the same DbContext — so combining it with correspondence approval in one transaction (ARCHITECTURE.md §5) can commit unrelated in-flight edits. And if a caller wraps it in an explicit transaction that later rolls back, the tracked OfficialNumber entity keeps the incremented LastSeq in memory while the database keeps the old value, so the next issue silently skips a number — which the AGREEMENT item 37 sequence-integrity check will later flag.
findings.fix: Document the transactional contract on IOfficialNumberService (caller opens db.Database.BeginTransaction, IssueAsync enlists), and after a failed/rolled-back outer transaction have the caller call db.Entry(row).Reload() — or expose an IssueAsync overload that takes the ambient IDbContextTransaction and reloads the official_numbers row on failure. At minimum add a comment and a walkthrough test in B3 that asserts no number is consumed when the surrounding approval rolls back.

findings.issue: Insert_OnSyncedTable_WritesChangeLogRow calls db.ChangeLog.IgnoreDeleted(). ChangeLogEntry is not a SyncedEntity and carries no query filter, so IgnoreQueryFilters is a no-op there — the call reads as if the change log were soft-delete filtered and will mislead the next reader.
findings.fix: Drop the IgnoreDeleted() call from that query (line 32); keep the plain `db.ChangeLog.Where(...)` form used by the other tests in the file.

findings.issue: Coverage gaps in otherwise strong tests: AuditService, ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddWakeelCore, WakeelPaths (the ARCHITECTURE.md §2 layout and VaultFilePath sharding) and the search_fts triggers/tokenizer have no tests at all. I verified search_fts manually (insert into search_chunks then `MATCH 'الامل'` returns 1, journal_mode=wal, foreign_keys=1, busy_timeout=5000), but nothing in the suite would catch a regression. EveryDbSet_IsQueryable also asserts only `Count >= 60` where the real contract is 66.
findings.fix: Add: an AuditService test asserting the row lands in audit_log with the Arabic summary and a details JSON that contains no secrets; an AddWakeelCore test building a ServiceProvider (with a WakeelDb registered from a temp DbSession) and resolving each registered interface; a WakeelPaths test asserting the §2 folder names and that VaultFilePath("ab12...") shards under vault\ab; an FTS test inserting a search_chunk with tashkeel and asserting a MATCH on the undiacritised term, plus update/delete keeping search_fts in step. Tighten the DbSet assertion to `Assert.Equal(66, setProperties.Count)`.

findings.issue: ApplyKey builds the key into a managed string (`PRAGMA key = "x'<hex>'"`) that is also retained by SqliteCommand.CommandText. Managed strings cannot be zeroed, so the 32-byte database key survives in the heap (and possibly the page file) for the process lifetime. The hex itself comes from Convert.ToHexString so there is no injection surface, and the key-length guard is correct.
findings.fix: Keep the current approach (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite offers no byte-oriented key API) but narrow the exposure: build the command text into a `char[]`/`Span<char>` and call `CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory` on it after ExecuteNonQuery where possible, dispose the command immediately (already done), and add an XML-doc note that the key string is unavoidably heap-resident so the process must never write a full memory dump to disk. Also state in the doc that callers should zero their own keyBytes after DbSession.Open/Unlock.

findings.issue: Plural uses Math.Abs(count), which throws OverflowException for int.MinValue, and maps count 0 to the broken-plural form ("0 مهام"). The 0 mapping is a defensible reading of a spec that names five buckets but supplies four strings, and the builder documented it, but the report generator (B5, AGREEMENT item 53c) will emit that text verbatim so it should be an explicit product decision rather than an implementation default. Normalize also collapses whitespace, which shifts character offsets relative to the original text and so cannot be used directly to locate OCR word boxes (ARCHITECTURE.md §8).
findings.fix: Replace Math.Abs(count) with `count == int.MinValue ? int.MaxValue : Math.Abs(count)` (or take a uint/long). Confirm the zero form with the supervisor and add an XML-doc line stating the chosen rendering. Add a remark on Normalize that it is index-destructive and that OCR highlighting must keep its own offset map.

missing_spec_items: Automatic maintenance of the SyncedEntity columns — nothing sets created_at/updated_at/origin_device or increments row_version, which DATA-MODEL.md §0 requires ("عداد يزيد عند كل تعديل محلي") and which ARCHITECTURE.md §6 date-range export depends on through the change_log triggers.

Enforcement of the ARCHITECTURE.md §5 / AGREEMENT item 5 rule across a year boundary: an official number with a date earlier than the last issued number is currently accepted when the earlier year has no official_numbers row (verified: 20270305/12001 then 20261120/12001).

The spec signature OfficialNumberService.Issue(kind, now): implemented as IssueAsync(kind, now, clockVerdict), so the ARCHITECTURE.md §9 clock check at issuance is delegated to the caller and unenforced inside Core.
ErrorMapper's SqliteException case is effectively unreachable — EF wraps provider failures in DbUpdateException, so real database errors map to the generic "unexpected" message (verified).
audit_log is annotated "يُزامَن كقراءة فقط" in DATA-MODEL.md §1 but has no change_log trigger and no sync columns, so it never reaches another device.
document_pages and document_links have no sync columns and no triggers, so OCR page text and document links never reach a second PC even though their parent documents row does.
Seventeen JSON column names deviate from DATA-MODEL.md (cc_json vs cc, details_json vs details, agenda_json vs agenda, …), and restore_log.details is inconsistent with audit_log.details_json.
No tests for AuditService, AddWakeelCore, WakeelPaths, or the search_fts virtual table and its three sync triggers (all of which are required by spec items 3, 4 and 5).
notes:
Commands run exactly as instructed, in D:\AI\Administration2:
- `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` → Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) (TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, so warnings-as-errors is clean).
- `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` → Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 106, Skipped: 0, Total: 106, 14 s.
No file in the repository was modified by this review (git status shows only the builder's own additions).

What is genuinely good and should be kept:
- The "EF model matches the SQL schema exactly" criterion holds in BOTH directions. I verified it independently of the builder's own check by parsing all 66 CREATE TABLE statements and all entity properties (applying the same snake_case rule and the SyncedEntity base columns) and diffing per table: 66 tables, 66 entities, zero sql-only and zero ef-only columns. Every DATA-MODEL.md §0–§12 table name is present; nothing is missing and nothing is extra.
- SQLCipher wiring is correct and I confirmed it at runtime on a fresh database: journal_mode=wal, foreign_keys=1, busy_timeout=5000, cipher_page_size=4096; a wrong key fails inside DbConnectionFactory.Open on the sqlite_master probe; the file header is not the plaintext SQLite magic. Disabling connection pooling is the right call and the comment explaining why is accurate — with pooling on, the wrong-key and re-key paths silently reuse an already-unlocked handle.
- No SQL injection surface: the only interpolated SQL is the PRAGMA key hex, which comes from Convert.ToHexString of a length-checked 32-byte array; every other statement is parameterised or a static literal, and the migration scripts are embedded resources.
- FTS5 works end to end: I inserted a search_chunks row and a MATCH query through the external-content table returned it, with the unicode61 / remove_diacritics 2 tokenizer and correct 'delete' commands in the update/delete triggers.
- The tests assert real behaviour rather than tautologies: EveryDbSet_IsQueryable materialises every column of every DbSet against the migrated database (so a missing column fails, not just a missing table); the numbering tests actually drive the sequence to 900 and 999; the cycle tests check the AGREEMENT item 52 example and leap/non-leap February; the soft-delete test checks both directions of the filter; the error-mapper tests regex-scan for Latin letters and Arabic/Western digits. The only weak assertion I found is `Count >= 60` instead of 66.
- The DateTime 'Z'-in-custom-format bug the builder found and documented is real and the diagnosis is right; the fix is just too narrow (see the Parse finding).

Verdict is `fix` rather than `accept` because of two high findings I confirmed by running code, not by reading it: (1) every SyncedEntity row written without hand-set stamps lands with created_at/updated_at = 0001-01-01 and origin_device = '' — and Core's own FinancialCycleService already does this — which makes the row invisible to the ARCHITECTURE.md §6 date-range sync export; and (2) an official number dated earlier than the last issued number is accepted across a year boundary. Both are cheap to fix and both are in the data layer that B3–B6 will build on, so they should be fixed before hand-off rather than after. The medium findings (DbUpdateException not unwrapped, brittle DateTime parsing, change_log.device semantics, unfiltered unique indexes vs the soft-delete filter, the 17 renamed JSON columns, and the caller-supplied clock verdict) are all contract-level and equally cheap now, expensive later.

Two items need a supervisor decision rather than a code change: the JSON column naming (amend DATA-MODEL.md or rename the columns — but stop the drift), and the change_log.device semantics (creating device vs editing device), which DATA-MODEL.md §11 leaves ambiguous."
